marking_schemes.question_text: State and define the S.I. unit of power.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: watt – If 1joule of work is done in 1 second then the power spent/developed/expended is 1watt.
key_points: Unit name: watt
Definition: power when 1 joule of work is done in 1 second
marking_schemes.model_answer: The S.I. unit of power is the watt. It is defined as the power spent or developed when 1 joule of work is done in 1 second.
common_errors: Did not define the unit or defined an incorrect unit
Spelling errors while stating and defining watt
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates answered correctly; some made spelling errors or gave incorrect definitions.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is the unit horse power related to the S.I. unit of power?
key_points: 1 H.P. = 746 W (or 750 W accepted)
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1 horse power = 746 W (also accepted as 750 W).
common_errors: Wrote 1 H.P. = 0.746 watt or 1 watt = 746 H.P.
Unsure about exact value of H.P. in watt
Did not write the unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this sub-part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the energy changes in the following cases while in use: An electric iron.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electrical energy to heat energy
key_points: Electrical energy converts to heat energy
marking_schemes.model_answer: In an electric iron, electrical energy is converted to heat energy.
common_errors: Stated electrical to mechanical or vice versa
Gave irrelevant answers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates stated incorrect energy change for the electric iron.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the energy changes in the following cases while in use: A ceiling fan.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electrical energy to kinetic/mechanical energy.
key_points: Electrical energy converts to kinetic/mechanical energy
marking_schemes.model_answer: In a ceiling fan, electrical energy is converted to kinetic (mechanical) energy.
common_errors: Stated energy change as mechanical to wind energy instead of electrical to kinetic energy
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly; some used incorrect energy names.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram below shows a lever in use (E is effort, L is load, F is fulcrum). To which class of levers does it belong?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Second order (or class) lever.
key_points: Second class lever
marking_schemes.model_answer: This is a second class (second order) lever.
common_errors: Wrote Class I or Class III lever instead of Class II
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote second class lever correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Without changing the dimensions of the lever, if the load is shifted towards the fulcrum what happens to the mechanical advantage of the lever?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Mechanical advantage of the lever increases.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mechanical advantage of the lever increases.
key_points: Load distance from fulcrum decreases, so MA increases
marking_schemes.model_answer: The mechanical advantage of the lever increases.
common_errors: Unable to answer correctly
Just mentioned mechanical advantage is greater than one without realizing it was already greater than one and increases further
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates were unable to answer this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is the ratio of the velocities of light of wavelengths 4000Å and 8000Å in vacuum 1:1?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: In vacuum their speed/velocity is the same.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: In vacuum their speed/velocity is the same.
key_points: Speed of light in vacuum is independent of wavelength
marking_schemes.model_answer: In vacuum, the speed of light is the same for all wavelengths, hence the ratio of their velocities is 1:1.
common_errors: Arrived at correct or incorrect answer after long unnecessary calculations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates were able to answer this question.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which of the above wavelengths (4000Å or 8000Å) has a higher frequency?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 4000 Å has higher frequency.
key_points: Frequency inversely proportional to wavelength
marking_schemes.model_answer: 4000 Å has the higher frequency since frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote 8000 Å incorrectly
Did huge unnecessary calculations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly as 4000 Å.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is the motion of a body moving with a constant speed around a circular path said to be accelerated?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Because on a circular path the direction of motion changes continuously which changes the velocity of the body continuously.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Because on a circular path the direction of motion changes continuously which changes the velocity of the body continuously.
key_points: Direction of motion changes continuously
Velocity is a vector, so continuous change in direction means continuous change in velocity, i.e., acceleration
marking_schemes.model_answer: Because on a circular path the direction of motion changes continuously, which changes the velocity of the body continuously, and this constitutes acceleration.
common_errors: Explained centripetal and centrifugal forces instead
Showed motion is tangential diagrammatically but did not clarify acceleration due to constant speed circular motion
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates were unable to make clear the concept correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the unit of physical quantity obtained by the formula 2K/V², where K: kinetic energy, V: Linear velocity.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: kg or kilogram/g/ any unit of mass
marking_schemes.scheme_text: kg or kilogram/g/ any unit of mass can be accepted.
key_points: 2K/V² gives mass, so unit is kg (or any mass unit)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The unit is kg (kilogram), or any unit of mass.
common_errors: Unable to name the unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates could name the unit correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: The power of a lens is –5D. Find its focal length.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: f = 1/P = 1/5 = 0.2 m or 20cm (substitution expressed with negative sign is also acceptable)
key_points: f = 1/P
f = 0.2 m or 20 cm
common_errors: Calculated focal length incorrectly
Expressed focal length in incorrect unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: The power of a lens is –5D. Name the type of lens.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concave/diverging lens
key_points: Negative power indicates concave/diverging lens
marking_schemes.model_answer: It is a concave (diverging) lens.
common_errors: Unaware that negative focal length sign indicates a concave lens
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates named the type of lens correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the position of the object in front of a converging lens if it produces a real and same size image of the object.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: at 2F
key_points: Object at 2F gives real, same size, inverted image
marking_schemes.model_answer: The object should be placed at 2F.
common_errors: Gave incorrect position
Drew incorrect diagram
Confused with labelling from Q6(b)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates gave the incorrect position of the object.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the position of the object in front of a converging lens if it is used as a magnifying lens.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Between the optical centre and principal focus.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Between the optical centre and principal focus.
key_points: Object between optical centre and F for magnifying use
marking_schemes.model_answer: The object should be placed between the optical centre and the principal focus.
common_errors: Made same error as in b(i)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority made the same error as in the previous sub-part.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the relation between the critical angle and the absolute refractive index of a medium.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: μ = 1/sin c
key_points: Refractive index = 1/sin(critical angle)
marking_schemes.model_answer: μ = 1/sin c, where c is the critical angle.
common_errors: Simply mentioned increases and decreases instead of exact mathematical relation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Only a few candidates wrote the correct mathematical relation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which colour of light has a higher critical angle? Red light or Green light.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Red
key_points: Red light has higher critical angle
marking_schemes.model_answer: Red light has a higher critical angle.
common_errors: Mentioned green which was incorrect
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote the correct colour.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define scattering.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Scattering is the absorption and then reemission of light without the change in the wavelength.
key_points: Absorption and reemission of light without change in wavelength
marking_schemes.model_answer: Scattering is the absorption and then re-emission of light by particles without any change in wavelength.
common_errors: Stated definition of dispersion instead
Did not state absorption and reemission without change in wavelength
Reversed order to reemission and absorption
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates stated the incorrect definition (dispersion instead of scattering).

marking_schemes.question_text: The smoke from a fire looks white. Which of the following statements is true? 1. Molecules of the smoke are bigger than the wavelength of light. 2. Molecules of the smoke are smaller than the wavelength of light.
options: 1. Molecules of the smoke are bigger than the wavelength of light.
2. Molecules of the smoke are smaller than the wavelength of light.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Statement 1
key_points: Smoke molecules bigger than wavelength causes white appearance
marking_schemes.model_answer: Statement 1 is true.
common_errors: A few candidates chose statement 2 as the correct option
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates identified the correct statement.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following diagram shows a 60°, 30°, 90° glass prism of critical angle 42°. Copy the diagram and complete the path of incident ray AB emerging out of the prism marking the angle of incidence on each surface.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bending away at surface XZ. Angle of incidence = 30°
key_points: Total internal reflection at YZ surface
Ray bends away from normal at surface XZ
Angle of incidence = 30° at second surface
marking_schemes.model_answer: The ray undergoes total internal reflection at surface YZ and emerges by bending away from the normal at surface XZ, with the angle of incidence at that surface being 30°.
common_errors: Showed ray bending towards normal instead of away
Ambiguous diagrams
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority showed total internal reflection; some drew ambiguous diagrams.

marking_schemes.question_text: Displacement distance graph of two sound waves A and B, travelling in a medium, are as shown in the diagram below. Study the two sound waves and compare their Amplitudes.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Amplitudes of A and B are in the ratio 2:1.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Amplitudes of A and B are in the ratio 2:1.
key_points: Ratio of amplitudes A:B = 2:1
marking_schemes.model_answer: The amplitudes of A and B are in the ratio 2:1.
common_errors: Compared using 'more or less' instead of exact ratio
Left answer in fractional form not reduced to lowest form
Stated raw values instead of ratio
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were unable to comprehend the diagram correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Displacement distance graph of two sound waves A and B, travelling in a medium, are as shown in the diagram below. Study the two sound waves and compare their Wavelengths.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Wavelengths of A and B are in the ratio 1:2.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Wavelengths of A and B are in the ratio 1:2.
key_points: Ratio of wavelengths A:B = 1:2
marking_schemes.model_answer: The wavelengths of A and B are in the ratio 1:2.
common_errors: Compared using 'more or less' instead of ratio
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Same errors as amplitude sub-part.

marking_schemes.question_text: You have three resistors of values 2Ω, 3Ω and 5Ω. How will you join them so that the total resistance is more than 7Ω? Draw a diagram for the arrangement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2Ω, 3Ω, 5Ω joined in series.
key_points: All three resistors connected in series
marking_schemes.model_answer: Connect the 2Ω, 3Ω, and 5Ω resistors in series.
common_errors: Showed a straight line instead of a wavy line to depict resistor
Showed various series-parallel combinations
Considered 7Ω as one of the resistors
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates showed incorrect diagrams.

marking_schemes.question_text: You have three resistors of values 2Ω, 3Ω and 5Ω. How will you join them so that the total resistance is more than 7Ω? Calculate the equivalent resistance.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: R = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω (Only 10 Ω can be accepted if the diagram is shown else substitution is a must.)
common_errors: Used parallel formula for series combination or vice versa
Tried to make resistance equal to 7Ω instead of more than 7Ω
Did not write the unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates overlooked the requirement of 'more than 7Ω'.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you understand by the term nuclear fusion?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Nuclear fusion – The process in which two lighter nuclei of lighter atoms combine to form a heavy and more stable nucleus with the liberation of large amount of heat.
key_points: Two lighter nuclei combine
Form heavier, more stable nucleus
Large amount of heat/energy released
marking_schemes.model_answer: Nuclear fusion is the process in which two lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier, more stable nucleus with the release of a large amount of energy.
common_errors: Wrote smaller and bigger atoms/nuclei instead of lighter and heavier nuclei
Wrote definition of nuclear fission instead
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates confused fusion with fission.

marking_schemes.question_text: Nuclear power plants use nuclear fission reaction to produce electricity. What is the advantage of producing electricity by fusion reaction?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The product formed is not radioactive hence less harmful to human/ energy produced per nucleon (for same mass of nuclear material) is more than fission.
key_points: Product not radioactive, less harmful
Energy produced per nucleon is more than fission
marking_schemes.model_answer: The product of fusion is not radioactive, making it less harmful to humans, and the energy produced per nucleon is greater than that of fission for the same mass of nuclear material.
common_errors: Expressed that only fission can produce electricity
Gave advantages of fission instead of fusion
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates were unable to answer this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you understand by free vibrations of a body?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Vibrations of a body in absence of any external periodic force with constant frequency and amplitude.
key_points: No external periodic force
Constant frequency
Constant amplitude
marking_schemes.model_answer: Free vibrations are vibrations of a body in the absence of any external periodic force, with constant frequency and constant amplitude.
common_errors: Did not write key words like 'without influence of external periodic force', 'constant frequency and constant amplitude'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates missed key definitional terms.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why does the amplitude of a vibrating body continuously decrease during damped vibrations?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: The energy is lost to the surrounding due to the friction of the surrounding medium.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The energy is lost to the surrounding due to the friction of the surrounding medium.
key_points: Energy lost to surroundings due to friction of the medium
marking_schemes.model_answer: The amplitude decreases because energy is lost to the surroundings due to friction/resistance of the surrounding medium.
common_errors: Did not mention that external force is resistive in nature or causes loss of energy
Wrote definition of damped vibrations instead
Wrote that damped vibrations are due to removal of external force
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates missed the resistive/energy loss aspect.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is the e.m.f. across primary and secondary coils of a transformer related with the number of turns of coil in them?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: e.m.f. and the number of turns of the coil are directly proportional.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: e.m.f. and the number of turns of the coil are directly proportional.
key_points: e.m.f. directly proportional to number of turns
marking_schemes.model_answer: The e.m.f. across the coils is directly proportional to the number of turns of the coil.
common_errors: Wrote how voltage/current increases or decreases in step-up/step-down transformer
Wrote E = Ns/Np without clear relation statement
Gave relation for only primary or only secondary coil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates were unable to answer this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: On which type of current do transformers work?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A.C. or alternating current.
key_points: Transformers work on alternating current (A.C.)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Transformers work on alternating current (A.C.).
common_errors: Wrote d.c or induced current or high voltage current or eddy currents
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates wrote incorrect current types.

marking_schemes.question_text: How can a temperature in degree Celsius be converted into S.I. unit of temperature?
key_points: Add 273 to Celsius temperature to get Kelvin
marking_schemes.model_answer: To convert Celsius to Kelvin, add 273 to the Celsius temperature: K = °C + 273.
common_errors: Wrote 1°C = 273 K incorrectly
Wrote t°C-273 or T = 273 - t°C or t = 273+K
Confused 1°C=1K
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates could not express the conversion correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: A liquid X has the maximum specific heat capacity and is used as a coolant in Car radiators. Name the liquid X.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Water
key_points: Water has maximum specific heat capacity
marking_schemes.model_answer: Water.
common_errors: Wrote hydrogen, kerosene, petrol or diesel incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates named the liquid correctly as water.

marking_schemes.question_text: A solid metal weighing 150 g melts at its melting point of 800°C by providing heat at the rate of 100 W. The time taken for it to completely melt at the same temperature is 4 min. What is the specific latent heat of fusion of the metal?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: P × t = mL => 100 × 4 × 60 = 150 × L (both side correct substitutions) = 160 J g-1 (answer is accepted in any unit.)
key_points: Correct substitution on both sides
marking_schemes.model_answer: Q = P × t = 100 × (4 × 60) = 24000 J. Using Q = mL: 24000 = 150 × L, so L = 160 J g⁻¹ (or equivalent in any consistent unit).
accepted_alternatives: Answer expressed in any consistent unit
common_errors: Used melting point 800°C incorrectly in calculation, substituting 150 × 800 × l
Used incorrect expressions Q = mcΔt only or Q = ml only or Q = ml + mcΔt
Wrote incorrect unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority incorrectly used the melting point value in their calculation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the wire used in a household circuit which is also called as the phase wire.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Live wire
key_points: Phase wire = live wire
marking_schemes.model_answer: Live wire.
common_errors: Unaware of the term 'phase'
Answered in terms of colours of wire
Wrote hot wire, live/earth, or neutral/earth
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates were unaware of the term 'phase'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the wire used in a household circuit which is connected to the top terminal of a three-pin socket.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Earth wire
key_points: Top terminal of three-pin socket = earth wire
marking_schemes.model_answer: Earth wire.
common_errors: Wrote live wire or live/neutral
Answered using colours of wire
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This question was attempted well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: What are isobars?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Elements of same mass number but different atomic numbers are called isobars.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Elements of same mass number but different atomic numbers are called isobars.
key_points: Same mass number, different atomic number
marking_schemes.model_answer: Isobars are elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers.
common_errors: Confused isobars with isotopes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates confused isobars and isotopes.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one example of isobars.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: ₆C¹⁴, ₇N¹⁴ or ₁₂Mg²³, ₁₁Na²³ (any one correct example)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 6C14, 7N14, 12Mg23, 11Na23 (Any one correct example)
key_points: Correct pair with same mass number, different atomic number
marking_schemes.model_answer: ₆C¹⁴ and ₇N¹⁴ are isobars (or ₁₂Mg²³ and ₁₁Na²³).
common_errors: Wrote examples with incorrect mass/atomic number
Wrote elements without atomic and mass numbers
Gave examples of isotopes instead
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates made errors in the example given.

marking_schemes.question_text: Derive a relationship between S.I. and C.G.S. unit of work.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 J = 1 N x 1 m; 1 J = 10^5 dyn x 100 cm; 1 J = 10^7 ergs
key_points: 1 J = 10^7 ergs
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1 J = 1 N × 1 m. Since 1 N = 10⁵ dyn and 1 m = 100 cm, 1 J = 10⁵ dyn × 100 cm = 10⁷ dyn·cm = 10⁷ ergs.
common_errors: Wrote the relation directly without deriving it
Showed derivation between newton and dyne only
Meaningless substitution on R.H.S.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates failed to properly derive the relation.

marking_schemes.question_text: A force acts on a body and displaces it by a distance S in a direction at an angle θ with the direction of force. What should be the value of θ to get the maximum positive work?
key_points: Maximum work when θ = 0° (cos θ = 1)
marking_schemes.model_answer: θ = 0°, since W = FS cos θ is maximum when cos θ = 1.
common_errors: Wrote θ = 90° or 180° or cos 90° = 1
Made contradictory statements like cos 0 = 0
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates gave incorrect angle values.

marking_schemes.question_text: A half metre rod is pivoted at the centre with two weights of 20 gf and 12 gf suspended at a perpendicular distance of 6 cm and 10 cm from the pivot respectively. Which of the two forces acting on the rigid rod causes clockwise moment?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 12 kg f
key_points: 12 gf causes clockwise moment
marking_schemes.model_answer: The 12 gf force causes the clockwise moment.
common_errors: Confused and wrote both 20 gf and 12 gf
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: A half metre rod is pivoted at the centre with two weights of 20 gf and 12 gf suspended at a perpendicular distance of 6 cm and 10 cm from the pivot respectively. Is the rod in equilibrium?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Yes
key_points: Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment: 20×6=120, 12×10=120, hence equilibrium
marking_schemes.model_answer: Yes, the rod is in equilibrium since the clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal (20×6 = 12×10 = 120 gf·cm).
common_errors: Arrived at conclusion after long unnecessary calculations
Guessed the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This part was attempted well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: The direction of 20 gf force is reversed. What is the magnitude of the resultant moment of the forces on the rod?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: On reversing the direction of 20 kg f, the magnitude of the resultant forces on the rod = 20 × 6 + 12 × 10 = 240
key_points: Both moments now act in the same direction: 20×6 + 12×10 = 240 gf·cm
marking_schemes.model_answer: On reversing the 20 gf force, both moments act in the same direction: Resultant moment = 20×6 + 12×10 = 240 gf·cm.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This question was performed well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw a diagram to show a block and tackle pulley system having a velocity ratio of 3 marking the direction of load(L), effort(E) and tension(T).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Two pulleys in block and one pulley (movable) in tackle, their proper connection, marking directions of load(L) and effort(E) and at least one tension and the support. Strands should be stretched.
key_points: Two fixed pulleys in block, one movable pulley in tackle
Correct labelling of L, E, T
Support shown
Strands stretched, not loose
marking_schemes.model_answer: A block and tackle system with two pulleys in the fixed block and one movable pulley in the tackle, properly connected with strands stretched, and load (L), effort (E), and tension (T) clearly marked, giving a velocity ratio of 3.
common_errors: Direction of load and tension missing
Incorrect number of pulleys in fixed/movable block
No distinction between fixed and movable block
No support shown
Strands shown loose
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Common anomalies included missing labels and incorrect pulley arrangement.

marking_schemes.question_text: The pulley system drawn lifts a load of 150 N when an effort of 60 N is applied. Find its mechanical advantage.
key_points: M.A. = Load/Effort = 150/60 = 2.5
common_errors: Left the answer in fraction form
Added units incorrectly
Vague calculations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority got the calculation correct but left it in fraction form.

marking_schemes.question_text: Is the above pulley system an ideal machine or not?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: No, it is not an ideal system.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: No, it is not an ideal system.
key_points: M.A. (2.5) is less than V.R. (3), so not ideal
marking_schemes.model_answer: No, it is not an ideal machine because the mechanical advantage (2.5) is less than the velocity ratio (3).
common_errors: Wrote it is an ideal pulley system incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly; some incorrectly stated it was ideal.

marking_schemes.question_text: A ray of light XY passes through a right angled isosceles prism as shown (45° angles). What is the angle through which the incident ray deviates and emerges out of the prism?
key_points: Deviation angle = 90°
marking_schemes.model_answer: The ray deviates by 90°.
common_errors: Reported the deviation angle as 0° or 45°
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered sub-parts well with some common mistakes.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the instrument where this action of the right angled isosceles prism is put into use.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: refracting periscope.
key_points: Instrument: refracting periscope
marking_schemes.model_answer: Refracting periscope.
common_errors: Named binoculars incorrectly as the instrument
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates named the wrong instrument.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which prism surface will behave as a mirror?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Surface AB
key_points: Hypotenuse surface AB acts as mirror due to total internal reflection
marking_schemes.model_answer: Surface AB acts as the mirror due to total internal reflection.
common_errors: Wrote surfaces BC and AC will behave as mirror
Wrote all three surfaces behave as mirror
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates identified the wrong surface.

marking_schemes.question_text: An object AB is placed between O and F1 on the principal axis of a converging lens. Copy the diagram and by using three standard rays starting from point A, obtain an image of the object AB.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Image of the object AB, using three standard rays starting from point A - virtual, erect, magnified image formed on the same side as the object.
key_points: Three standard rays drawn correctly from point A
Refracted rays pass through correct focal points
Virtual image shown with dotted lines on same side as object
Arrows on incident and refracted rays
marking_schemes.model_answer: Using the three standard rays (parallel to axis refracting through F2, through optical centre undeviated, and through F1 emerging parallel to axis), the image formed for an object between O and F1 is virtual, erect, and magnified, located on the same side as the object.
common_errors: Ray after refraction did not pass through F
Virtual intersection/image not shown with dotted lines
Arrows missing on incident or refracted rays
Only two rays drawn, image not drawn
Arrows incorrectly drawn on dotted lines
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were unsure about the third standard ray.

marking_schemes.question_text: An object is placed at a distance of 12 cm from a convex lens of focal length 8 cm. Find the position of the image.
key_points: Use lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f
u = -12 cm, f = 8 cm
v = +24 cm
marking_schemes.model_answer: Using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, with u = -12 cm and f = 8 cm: 1/v = 1/8 - 1/12 = 1/24, so v = +24 cm.
common_errors: Used incorrect lens formula
Incorrect use of sign convention
Incorrect substitutions
Incorrect answer with correct unit or vice versa
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates were unable to answer this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: An object is placed at a distance of 12 cm from a convex lens of focal length 8 cm. Find the nature of the image.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Real, inverted, and bigger than the object.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Real or inverted; Image is bigger than object.
key_points: Real image
Inverted image
Image is bigger (magnified) than object
marking_schemes.model_answer: The image is real, inverted, and bigger than the object (since v > 2f is not the case here, but object is between F and 2F, image forms beyond 2F, magnified).
common_errors: Incorrect characteristics of the image given
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Errors linked to incorrect position calculation carried forward here.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the diagram of a right angled isosceles prism which is used to make an inverted image erect.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diagram showing object and image with two total internal reflections at 45° surfaces, i > c marked. (Any other correct ray diagram)
key_points: Two right-angled isosceles prisms used
Total internal reflection shown at 45° surfaces
90° deviation and inversion shown
Arrows on incident, refracted/reflected, and emergent rays
marking_schemes.model_answer: A diagram showing light undergoing total internal reflection at the 45° surfaces of two right-angled isosceles prisms arranged to invert and erect the image, with all rays properly labelled with arrows.
accepted_alternatives: Any other correct ray diagram achieving the same result
common_errors: Did not show 90° deviation
Did not show inversion of image
Missing arrows on incident, refracted, reflected and emergent rays
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates performed well barring a few exceptions.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram shows a wire stretched over a sonometer. Stems of two vibrating tuning forks A and B are touched to the wooden box. The paper rider just vibrates when tuning fork A is touched. Name the phenomenon when the paper rider just vibrates.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Forced vibrations
key_points: Paper rider vibrating (not flying off) indicates forced vibrations
marking_schemes.model_answer: Forced vibrations.
common_errors: Wrote damped and forced or resonant vibrations incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: The paper rider flies off when tuning fork B is touched to the box. Name the phenomenon when the paper rider flies off.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Resonance.
key_points: Paper rider flying off indicates resonance
marking_schemes.model_answer: Resonance.
common_errors: Wrote forced vibrations incorrectly instead of resonance
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why does the paper rider fly off when the stem of tuning fork B is touched to the box?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Frequency of the tuning fork B matches the natural frequency of the stretched wire and vibrates with greater amplitude.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Frequency of the tuning fork B matches the natural frequency of the stretched wire and vibrates with greater amplitude.
key_points: Frequency of tuning fork B matches natural frequency of wire
Wire vibrates with greater amplitude at resonance
marking_schemes.model_answer: Because the frequency of tuning fork B matches the natural frequency of the stretched wire, causing it to vibrate with much greater amplitude (resonance), making the paper rider fly off.
common_errors: Stated frequency becomes more than natural frequency instead of matching it
Missing explanation of increased amplitude
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates missed the amplitude explanation.

marking_schemes.question_text: A person is standing at the sea shore. An observer on a ship anchored between a vertical cliff and the person fires a gun. The person hears two sounds, 2 seconds and 3 seconds after seeing the smoke. Speed of sound = 320 ms⁻¹. Calculate the distance between the observer on the ship and the person on the shore.
key_points: Direct sound heard 2s after seeing smoke
common_errors: Calculation mistakes

marking_schemes.question_text: A person is standing at the sea shore. An observer on a ship anchored between a vertical cliff and the person fires a gun. The person hears two sounds, 2 seconds and 3 seconds after seeing the smoke. Speed of sound = 320 ms⁻¹. Calculate the distance between the cliff and the observer on the ship.
key_points: Echo heard 1s after direct sound (3-2=1s), representing round trip to cliff
marking_schemes.model_answer: The echo from the cliff arrives 1 s after the direct sound (3-2=1s). d = (v×t)/2 = (320×1)/2 = 160 m.
common_errors: Calculation mistakes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this part well with some calculation errors.

marking_schemes.question_text: A fuse is rated 8A. Can it be used with an electrical appliance rated 5 KW, 200 V? Give a reason.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: I = P/V = 5000/200 = 25 A. No, it cannot be used. Maximum current drawn by the appliance is greater than the fuse rating.
key_points: Current exceeds fuse rating of 8A, so cannot be used
marking_schemes.model_answer: I = P/V = 5000/200 = 25 A. No, this fuse cannot be used because the current drawn by the appliance (25 A) is much greater than the fuse rating (8 A).
common_errors: Answered without calculating current
Made calculation errors
Did not comprehend meaning of 'fuse rating'
Simply wrote 'No' without reason
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Sub-parts were correctly attempted by most candidates except a few calculation/comprehension errors.

marking_schemes.question_text: An electric iron is rated 220V, 2kW. If the iron is used for 2h daily find the cost of running it for one week if it costs ₹4.25 per kWh.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: E = P x t = 2 x 2 = 4 kWh [Correct substitution]. Cost for running it for a week = 4 x 7 x 4.25 = ₹119/-
key_points: Daily energy = P × t = 2 kW × 2 h = 4 kWh
Weekly energy = 4 × 7 = 28 kWh
marking_schemes.model_answer: Daily energy = 2 kW × 2 h = 4 kWh. Weekly energy = 4 × 7 = 28 kWh. Cost = 28 × 4.25 = ₹119.
common_errors: Calculation errors
Did not account for one week (7 days)
Converted kW into watt unnecessarily
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Common lapses included not considering the weekly time period.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is the fuse absolutely necessary in a power circuit?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Power circuits draw large amount of current/ Electric shock in this circuit is very fatal hence to avoid it fuse is necessary in the power circuit/ to safeguard.
key_points: Power circuits draw large currents
Fuse protects against fatal electric shock/fire hazard
marking_schemes.model_answer: Power circuits draw a large amount of current, and electric shock or fire hazards from such circuits can be fatal; hence, a fuse is absolutely necessary to safeguard the circuit and prevent damage.

marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates could not correctly explain fuse necessity in power circuits.

key_points: Latent heat of fusion/melting

marking_schemes.question_text: State two differences between 'Heat Capacity' and 'Specific Heat Capacity'.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Heat capacity: heat absorbed by the mass of a body to raise its temperature by 1°C, S.I. Unit J K-1, depends on mass and specific heat capacity/material. Specific heat capacity: heat absorbed by unit mass of a body to raise its temperature by 1°C, S.I. unit J kg-1 K-1, does not depend on mass (but depends on material). (Any two points)
key_points: Heat capacity is for the whole body's mass; specific heat capacity is per unit mass
Different SI units: J K⁻¹ vs J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹
Heat capacity depends on mass; specific heat capacity does not depend on mass
marking_schemes.model_answer: Heat capacity is the heat absorbed by the mass of a body to raise its temperature by 1°C (unit: J K⁻¹) and depends on mass and material. Specific heat capacity is the heat absorbed by unit mass to raise temperature by 1°C (unit: J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) and depends only on the material, not the mass.
common_errors: Errors in definitions
Incorrect units stated
Did not write corresponding points of difference
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates made errors in the definitions and units.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a mathematical relation between Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Heat capacity (C') = mass of the body (m) x specific heat capacity (c)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Heat capacity(C') = mass of the body(m) x specific heat capacity (c)
key_points: C' = m × c
marking_schemes.model_answer: Heat capacity (C') = mass (m) × specific heat capacity (c).
common_errors: Confused symbols such as C, C' and H without explaining them
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates used symbols inconsistently.

marking_schemes.question_text: The temperature of 170g of water at 50°C is lowered to 5°C by adding certain amount of ice to it. Find the mass of ice added. Given: Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg-1 °C-1 and Specific latent heat of ice = 336000 J kg-1.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: mw cw θw = mi L + mi cw θw; 170 x 4.2 x 45 = mi [336 + 4.2 x 5]; mi = 90 g
key_points: Heat lost by water = Heat gained by ice (melting) + heat gained by melted ice to reach final temp
mi = 90 g
marking_schemes.model_answer: Heat lost by water = heat gained by ice. mw·cw·θw = mi·L + mi·cw·θw. 170 × 4.2 × 45 = mi[336 + 4.2×5]. Solving, mi = 90 g.
common_errors: Required conversions were not done
Proper equation was not formed
Heat absorbed by melted ice was not considered
Unit was incorrect or not mentioned in final answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Common inaccuracies included not accounting for heat absorbed by melted ice.

marking_schemes.question_text: The ore of Uranium found in nature contains 92U238 and 92U235. Although both isotopes are fissionable, one is more easily fissionable. Name the isotope of Uranium which is easily fissionable.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason why 92U235 is more easily fissionable than 92U238.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fission of 92U238 is possible only by fast neutrons while the fission of 92U235 can be even possible by the slow neutrons.
key_points: U-238 fissions only with fast neutrons
